articles.title: Ben Shelef to talk on Space Elevators
articles.summary: Ben Shelef, founder of the Spaceward Foundation, is scheduled to speak on November 12, 2005, about the development of space elevators. His talk will detail how advances in materials science are making these once-fanciful 'beanstalks' a plausible and significantly more cost-effective alternative to rockets for accessing space. The Spaceward Foundation is actively fostering this technology through initiatives like NASA grants and the Space Elevator Games.

articles.title: Fall Swap – November 13, 2005
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) is hosting its fifth annual Fall Astronomical Swap Meet on November 13, 2005, at Houge Park in San Jose. The event provides an opportunity for enthusiasts to buy and sell a wide array of astronomical equipment and related items, with sellers paying a 10% commission on sales. Attendees are encouraged to promote the swap meet to attract new members to the astronomy community and can utilize a consignment table for smaller items.

articles.title: The Shallow Sky: All Mars, All the Time
articles.summary: This article focuses on the optimal viewing of Mars throughout November, detailing its opposition, visible surface features like Syrtis Major and Hellas, and the changing views due to its rotation. Observers are encouraged to watch for phenomena such as the polar caps and various dark areas, with specific guidance on what features appear at different times of the month. It also briefly mentions the visibility of Venus, Uranus, Neptune, Saturn, and Jupiter during the same period.

articles.title: Mike Koop Receives AANC Amateur Astronomer Award
articles.summary: Mike Koop received the 2005 Astronomical Association of Northern California Amateur Astronomer Award for his extensive contributions to the astronomy community. He has been a fixture at both AANC and the San Jose Astronomical Association, serving in leadership roles and tirelessly managing the SJAA telescope loaner program, organizing mirror-making workshops, and handling club insurance issues. Koop is celebrated for his selfless dedication and significant impact on local astronomy clubs.

articles.title: NASA Space Place: Where No Spacecraft Has Gone Before
articles.summary: NASA's Voyager 1 spacecraft, launched in 1977, successfully completed its planetary flybys of Jupiter and Saturn, making significant discoveries before being slingshot into deep space. As of 2005, it has entered the heliosheath, a turbulent region where the Sun's solar wind piles up against the interstellar medium, acting as a crucial shield against galactic cosmic rays. Voyager 1 is exploring this never-before-visited area and is expected to reach interstellar space in 8-10 years.

articles.title: Silicon Valley Astronomy Lecture Series: Chris McKay to talk on November 9, 2005
articles.summary: Dr. Chris McKay of NASA's Ames Research Center will present a non-technical, illustrated talk titled "REVEALING TITAN" on November 9, 2005, as part of the Silicon Valley Astronomy Lecture Series. He will share the Cassini Mission's latest discoveries about Saturn's giant moon Titan, including findings from the probe that landed on its surface. The free public lecture will be held at Foothill College, and the document also includes solar system statistics for November 2005.

articles.title: SJAA loaner scope status
articles.summary: The article details the status of the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) loaner scope program, listing telescopes available for immediate loan, those currently on loan, and scopes with extended loan periods. SJAA members can borrow any available scope by contacting Mike Koop, with contact information provided for inquiries and pick-ups at SJAA events. The document also includes waiting lists for popular scopes.
